reasons: The principle of residential use of the first-floor and attic levels is acceptable because the site lies within Doncaster City Centre and the Primary Shopping Area, where residential uses on upper floors are supported subject to amenity considerations, in accordance with Doncaster Local Plan Policies 1 and 23.

The external alterations, including modifying the full-height window opening to form a door and removing the unauthorised roller shutter, are considered acceptable and would enhance the character and appearance of the High Street Conservation Area, according with Doncaster Local Plan Policies 37, 41, 42 and 44 and NPPF paragraph 135.

The proposal would provide substandard refuse and recycling access arrangements because future occupiers would have no direct access from the flat to the rear bin store and would need to access it either through the restaurant or by a convoluted route via public streets. This would represent poor design and would be contrary to NPPF paragraph 135 and Doncaster Local Plan Policies 10 and 44.

The applicant has failed to demonstrate that noise from the ground-floor restaurant and surrounding licensed commercial premises could be adequately mitigated to protect the amenity of future occupiers. The submitted noise information was generic rather than site-specific, contrary to NPPF paragraph 135 and Doncaster Local Plan Policies 10 and 44.

The proposed access to the cycle storage in the rear yard would be indirect and convoluted, requiring occupiers to leave the flat via Foundry Court and use a rear access route, which would deter regular use and fail to promote cycling as a sustainable travel mode, contrary to NPPF paragraph 117 and Doncaster Local Plan Policy 16.

The proposed flat would exceed the Nationally Described Space Standards for a one-bedroom two-person flat and, as amended, would provide an acceptable level of daylight and outlook when considered as a whole, according with Doncaster Local Plan Policy 45.

The proposal would not give rise to unacceptable impacts on existing neighbouring amenity because of the commercial nature of the surrounding area and the absence of residential overlooking issues, according with Doncaster Local Plan Policy 44.

The absence of off-street car parking is acceptable given the highly sustainable city centre location and good public transport links, and would not result in an unacceptable highway safety impact, in accordance with NPPF paragraph 116 and Doncaster Local Plan Policies 13 and 42.
The site is in Flood Zone 1 and therefore at low probability of flooding, so no flood risk concerns arise.
